.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Cooler and less humid this afternoon; warmer 
and more humid Sunday with isolated afternoon thunderstorms. 

High pressure will pass north of the area this afternoon and 
then off the Mid Atlantic coast Sunday. It will be slightly 
cooler and less humid this afternoon on NNW winds. As a result,
most areas should remain dry and seasonable this afternoon, 
although an inverted surface trough may result in isolated 
showers along the Allegheny Mountains. Southerly flow returns 
Sunday, bringing increasing heat and humidity. A passing 
shortwave trough may support a few afternoon showers and 
thunderstorms about anywhere.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Late summer heat returns next week.

Guidance remains steadfast on late summer heat returning to end 
meteorological summer (June 1-August 31) and begin meteorological 
autumn (September 1-November 30).

A strong mid-level ridge will build across the southern CONUS and 
into the Mid-Atlantic beginning on Sunday, and persist through at 
least the middle of the week. Some guidance has been trending 
towards having the ridge axis a bit further south and west, which 
would lower heights a bit and introduce more chances for showers and 
thunderstorms at times in large scale NW flow aloft. This lends to a 
bit of spread in the temperature forecast, especially if any back-
door surface cold fronts slide into the region by mid/late week.

Despite the uncertainties, it remains likely that high temperatures 
will reach the lower to middle 90s for much of the region for much 
of the upcoming week. Depending on smaller scale details, dew points 
could end up a little higher or lower than currently progged which 
will ultimately affect how high heat index values get. Values 
approaching Heat Advisory criteria (100-104 west of the Blue Ridge, 
105-109 east of the Blue Ridge) can't be ruled out, but the more 
likely scenario is for heat indices a bit below those values.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Thunderstorm chances increase next week.

Disturbances rounding a ridge to the south and west in NW flow aloft 
will introduce shower and thunderstorm chances at times next week. 
The timing and amplitude of these waves have very low predictability 
beyond a couple days in advance (at best). But the general theme 
will be enhanced lift and shear clashing with an increasingly hot 
and unstable airmass over or near the Mid-Atlantic. AI/ML guidance 
has broad elevated probabilities of severe weather much of next 
week, the details (including timing and magnitude/potential impact) 
of which will be ironed out in the coming days.

It should be noted that there is a conditional potential for one or 
more organized clusters of strong to severe storms at some point 
next week. The most likely time currently appears to be around mid 
week, but changes are to be expected at this time range.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
VFR conditions this afternoon through Monday. Isolated t-storms
possible Sunday afternoon. 

Prevailing VFR expected through early next week, with PM TS and 
early AM valley fog possibly introducing restrictions at times. 
Winds will generally be S/SW (except briefly NW Mon) 5-10 kts.

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions possible again Sunday night into Monday morning 
in southerly channeling.

Some southerly channeling could result in at or near SCA criteria 
gusts Sunday evening into early Monday morning. Additional bouts of 
channeling may be possible by mid next week.
